transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to walk through model selection options — we're evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
00:08 Maya Chen: Great, thanks Lena. I'm Maya, I'm the account lead, and Diego from our SE team will handle the technical details. Quick agenda: current stack, workloads, latency & cost targets, multilingual needs, tool-calling, and next steps. Sound good?
00:20 Samir Patel: Yep, that's perfect. Quick context — we run a customer support assistant and an insights extraction pipeline. Mixed English/Spanish, some Japanese cases, roughly 1.2k users active, peak 120 qps, but most of our traffic is bursts.
00:35 Jordan Li: From infra we're focused on data residency and KMS integration; some PII flows, so encryption at rest and audit logs are musts.
00:44 Diego Ramirez: Understood. Couple clarifying q's: typical prompt length, expected context windows, and whether you need tool or function calling like DB lookups or agent flows?
00:52 Samir: Typical prompt+history is 2-3k tokens but we have use cases that need 32k-ish context — long docs and multi-doc summaries. We also plan tool-calls for live inventory and agent routing.
01:05 Priya Rao: Also multilingual — about 20% Spanish, 5% Japanese; translation isn't perfect so model selection matters.
01:14 Maya: Thanks. On the context length: Redwood supports variants with extended context profiles; hosted models and dedicated pools can run 32k context models, but there are tradeoffs in latency and cost. Diego, can you talk about the performance side?
01:25 Diego: Sure. For very long context (32k) the common pattern is to use a model with native long-context support or chunk + retrieval. On GPU inference, longer sequences increase per-token compute nonlinearly, so cost goes up. We recommend two prongs: 1) run a dedicated 32k-capable model for the heavy long-doc flows, 2) use retrieval+shorter context for chat to keep latency low.
01:42 Lena: How does that map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? If we go Dedicated, are we pinned to a model family?
01:49 Diego: With Dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and can pin runtime images with selected model families — gives predictable throughput and you can enable quantization profiles we vet. Hosted is easier to start and we manage the pool; we offer verified model catalog with performance profiles. Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives you control over network/KMS and full audit capability, but has longer setup time and an enterprise contract.
02:10 Samir: Do you support tool-calling / function calling? We need structured outputs from the model and the ability to call back to our inventory API.
02:17 Diego: Yes — we support function/tool calling and streaming. There's a function-calling surface that can be run in all three modes. For Dedicated and Private you can run routing rules to keep certain requests within private variants. A note: tool-calling sometimes requires model prompt engineering and occasionally small latency hits.
02:33 Jordan: On security — SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and KMS. Do you have SOC2? How long is the attestation?
02:41 Maya: Redwood has SOC2 type II. We'll send the whitepaper and SOC2 packet. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. Also support for SAML and SCIM provisioning.
02:52 Priya: For multilingual accuracy, do you recommend a single multilingual open model, or separate language-specific models?
03:00 Diego: It depends. Some open models have strong multilingual capacity; others are better in English. A common approach: a single high-quality multilingual base for chat, and language-specific tuned variants for high-value workflows. We can run comparative evals on your Spanish/Japanese corpora during the pilot.
03:15 Lena: Competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI were mentioned earlier — how do Redwood's open models compare on cost and tool-calling?
03:22 Maya: We surface curated open models and give performance/latency profiles. Compared to hosted APIs from Anthropic/OpenAI, using Redwood Hosted with open models can be cheaper per token and gives model selection flexibility. Dedicated reduces variability and further improves unit economics for high qps.
03:36 Samir: For our peak 120 qps bursts, is Dedicated necessary? Could we start hosted and move later?
03:43 Diego: Many customers start Hosted to validate the workload; if steady throughput and strict latency SLAs are needed, moving to Dedicated is common. We also have burst policies — Dedicated can be configured with burst capacity. Hosted has autoscaling but may have softer latency SLOs at extreme peaks.
03:59 Jordan: Bandwidth/egress concerns for Private — our security team insists on VPC peering and on-prem options.
04:06 Maya: Private deployment supports VPC-to-VPC peering and on-prem packages. We'll need to go through the security questionnaire and a network runbook.
04:15 Samir: About quantization and accuracy — we've seen accuracy drop on 4-bit models for some of our extraction tasks. Can Redwood run quantized configs that keep accuracy?
04:23 Diego: Yes, our Optimize team has quantization profiles per workload. We can test INT8/4-bit variants in the pilot and measure regressions on your eval prompts. Often we can preserve accuracy for extraction tasks with per-layer calibration.
04:38 Priya: For the pilot, what telemetry will we get? Token-level cost, latency, per-route dashboards?
04:45 Maya: Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, latency percentiles, traces, and error logs. For Dedicated/Private you can also ship to your Prometheus/Grafana or Sumo for long-term retention.
04:58 Lena: Ok practical next steps — we want a 48-hour pilot that runs our Spanish + English chat flows and a long-doc summarization job on a 32k model. Can Redwood set that up?
05:08 Diego: Yes — we can spin a short Dedicated trial or Hosted with a 32k variant. For the benchmark we'll need your sample prompts, expected qps, and an eval sheet. I'll prepare the template.
05:20 Samir: Great. Also want an estimate of unit cost for the long-doc summarization at different quantization levels.
05:27 Maya: We'll include costing examples in the pricing sheet.
05:30 Jordan: Who's the contact for SOC2 and security attestation?
05:33 Maya: I'll be the contact — I'll share the security packet and a link to our compliance docs.
05:39 Priya: Slight note — transcription: we sometimes saw "KV cache" and "K-V cache" — can you clarify how stateful conversations are handled across calls?
05:46 Diego: Redwood manages KV cache in the runtime; session-level caches and prefix caching are supported to reduce cost. For privacy you can control cache retention and eviction policies.
05:56 Lena: Anything else?
05:58 Maya: Quick recap of owners and timeline: Maya send pricing & SOC2 by 4/1; Diego share benchmark by 4/2; customer sends corpora and qps by 4/3; schedule deep dive for infra.
06:10 Samir: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
06:12 Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the calendar invite and pilot instructions.
06:18 [meeting ends — recording stopped]
